append.text: **Ps 6:6, the test D5 named:** *no inferno, porém, quem vos dará graças?* — holds: the dative is kept (*vos*), it is as natural as MS1932's and DM1962's *louvará*, and it closes on a paroxytone; the Latinist passed it twice, neither the stylist nor the blind reader remarked on it.

**Tried on Ps 6, as asked:** the psalm has (con)turbáre four times — bones, soul, eye, enemies (6:3, 4, 8, 11; ταράσσω each time) — and *perturbar* carries all four: *os meus ossos estão perturbados … a minha alma está muito perturbada … O meu olho está perturbado pelo furor … fiquem muito perturbados*. The stylist: "as repetições sustentam bem a súplica", and no remark on bones or eye; the blind reader heard the bones as aching or the body shaken. Option for the eye alone: *se turvou* (MS1932). 6:3b returns in 30:11 (*ossa mea conturbáta sunt*).

**Ps 6:5 finds a place where it fails:** *éripe ánimam meam* with no source named — the only such *éripe* of the 17 in the psalter (grep) — would be *arrancai a minha alma*, "tear out my soul". Ps 6 has *libertai a minha alma* (this row's own alternative; DM1962's verb; safe: past *libertei*). Wherever a *de …* follows, or the object is *me*, *arrancar* is untouched. If one verb is wanted everywhere, *libertar* is the one that never fails; it stays apart from *liberáre* → livrar only by a suffix.

**Ps 6:5, 6:11:** *Voltai-vos, Senhor* (the formula: 79:15, 89:13 *Convértere, Dómine, úsquequo?* → *Voltai-vos, Senhor, até quando?*; safe: past *voltei*) … *que se voltem* (6:11 *convertántur*, nothing added: the blind reader heard retreat, turning to God and merely turning round — the Latin's three). The echo between the two ends of the psalm is kept.

**Ps 6:10 meets an object that is not a person:** *Dóminus oratiónem meam suscépit* (προσεδέξατο, not ἀντελάβετο) — *amparou a minha oração* props the prayer up. See the new open row *suscípere (a thing as object)*; D19 stands for persons.

**Ps 6:10 proposes the noun → *prece*:** *súplica* is a proparoxytone and the noun stands at a cadence in 11 of its 14 verses (*deprecatiónem meam* 6:10, 16:1a, 38:13, 54:2, 60:2, 141:7; *vocem deprecatiónis meæ* 27:6, 65:19, 85:6, 129:2b, 139:7) — rule 4. *O Senhor escutou a minha prece, * o Senhor acolheu a minha oração*: a plain word of its own beside *oração*, of the root of *precári*; passed all three readers. The verb stays *suplicar*. Wants a ruling before Ps 16.

**Ps 6:11 is the first *erubéscere*, and *corar* holds:** *Que todos os meus inimigos corem … e corem muito depressa* — the Latin's own image (to redden), bare; the blind reader took it at once for shame, the stylist kept it twice in his own rebuilt line, the Latinist passed it. See the new row *erubéscere*.

terms: | árguere | acusar (*não me acuseis no vosso furor*) | open | Ps 6:2 = 37:2; 5 verses (6:2, 37:2, 49:8, 49:21 *árguam te, et státuam contra fáciem tuam*, 93:10). L&S: with a person, "to accuse, reprove, censure, charge with" (*arguisse accusasse et convicisse*, Dig.); ἐλέγχω. *Repreender* (DRB *rebuke*, DM1962) is what the ear expects but is *increpáre*'s word (ἐπιτιμάω, 12 verses), and *repreendais* has a hiatus at the stress; *accusáre* does not occur in the psalter; MS1932 *arguir* is an examiner's verb in Brazil. No reader objected. **Gustavo's ear wanted: it opens two Penitential Psalms** |

| corrípere | castigar (*nem me castigueis na vossa ira*) | open | Ps 6:2 = 37:2; 7 verses (38:12, 89:10, 93:10 *Qui córripit gentes, non árguet?*, 104:14, 140:5 *Corrípiet me justus in misericórdia, et increpábit me*). Shares the word with *castigáre* (117:18) on D15's test: one Greek verb (παιδεύω — checked for 117:18 in the parallels) and the two never meet (*castigáre* has no other verse). *Corrigir* is *corrígere*'s (17:36b, 95:10, 118:9). MS1932, DRB *chastise* |

| infírmus | enfermo (*porque estou enfermo*) | open | Ps 6:3, answered by *sana me* → *curai-me*; MS1932. The family mostly says weakness (*infirmári* 9:4, 25:1, 26:2, 108:24 *génua mea infirmáta sunt* → enfraquecer) but 102:3 *sanat omnes infirmitátes tuas* → enfermidades; DRB *weak* is the option. Masculine in the Latin too |

| sanáre | curar (*curai-me, Senhor*) | open | Ps 6:3; 7 verses (29:3, 40:5 *sana ánimam meam*, 59:4, 102:3, 106:20, 146:3); the plain verb (DM1962), safe (past *curei*); MS1932 *sarar* is in Brazil mostly what the patient does |

| valde / veheménter | muito (both) | open | Ps 6:4, 6:11. Draft 1 kept them apart (*grandemente*); the stylist found it heavy. Merged on D15's test — σφόδρα all three times in this psalm — and it lets 6:11 *muito perturbados* answer 6:4 *muito perturbada*. *veheménter* elsewhere (20:2, 46:10, 103:1, 104:24, 118:140, 167) may want *grandemente* locally |
| úsquequo | até quando | working | Ps 4:3, Ps 6:4 *mas vós, Senhor, até quando?* — the broken question left broken; 10 verses |

| inférnus / ínferi | inferno | open | Ps 6:6 *no inferno, porém, quem vos dará graças?* — the Latin's word, kept (DRB *hell*). **The blind reader heard the hell of the damned first, the world of the dead second.** In 6:6 both are true; the hard tests are 15:10 *non derelínques ánimam meam in inférno* and 138:8 *si descéndero in inférnum, ades*; 19 verses. Options: *os infernos* (the old plural for the abode of the dead — the Creed's wording, from memory, unverified), *a mansão dos mortos* (the Creed as now said in Brazil — unverified; a paraphrase), MS1932 *habitação dos mortos*, DM1962 *limbos*. Heavy: wants a ruling |
| memor esse (+ genitive) | lembrar-se de | working | Ps 6:6 *quem se lembre de vós*; as Ps 118:49, 52, 55 |

| laboráre | cansar-se (*Cansei-me gemendo*) | open | Ps 6:7; ἐκοπίασα; 68:4 *Laborávi clamans* → *Cansei-me clamando*; 48:9, 126:1a *in vanum laboravérunt* will want *trabalhar*. *Cansei-me no meu gemido* failed the stylist; his *Cansei-me de gemer* is heard as "I have had enough of" |
| gémitus | gemido | working | Ps 6:7 (as a gerund there); 8 verses |

| lectus / stratum | leito / cama | open | Ps 6:7 *o meu leito … a minha cama* (DM1962's pair); *lectus* shares *leito* with *cubíle* (Ps 4:5), which it never meets; 40:4 follows (*sobre o leito da sua dor … toda a sua cama*), 62:7 *super stratum meum*; **131:3 *in lectum strati mei* cannot** and decides locally |
| lácrimæ / fletus | lágrimas / pranto | working | Ps 6:7, 6:9 *a voz do meu pranto* (MS1932, DM1962) |
| rigáre | regar | working | Ps 6:7; 103:13 |
| inveteráre | envelhecer | working | Ps 6:8 *envelheci entre todos os meus inimigos*; 17:46, 31:3 |

| *a furóre* (6:8) | pelo furor | open | the Latin names no owner; with the article it may point back to 6:2 *no vosso furor*. The blind reader heard the speaker's own rage first, the Lord's second, the enemies' third |

| discédere a | afastar-se de (*Afastai-vos de mim*) | open | Ps 6:9 (DM1962 word for word); the imperative only here; stays apart from *declináre a* → apartar-se de (118:115, a near twin); shares the verb with the transitive *amovére / repéllere* → afastar |

| suscípere (a thing as object) | acolher (*o Senhor acolheu a minha oração*) | open | Ps 6:10. D19's *amparar* was made on persons; with a prayer (6:10), mercy (47:10 *Suscépimus, Deus, misericórdiam tuam*) or peace (71:3 *Suscípiant montes pacem*) as object it fails, and the Greek changes verb too (προσδέχομαι in 6:10). *Acolher* is the nearest neighbour of *amparar*; *receber* (MS1932, DRB) is the option. 16:12 *Suscepérunt me sicut leo* (hostile) will need a third |

| erubéscere | corar | open | Ps 6:11, twice; D15's proposal tried and it holds (see *confúndi*); 9 verses; 82:18 *Erubéscant … et confundántur* → *Corem … e sejam envergonhados*. Options *corar de vergonha*, *envergonhar-se* (differs from *confúndi* only in voice) |
| velóciter | depressa (*muito depressa*) | working | Ps 6:11; 7 verses; *velóciter exáudi me* (68:18, 101:3, 142:7a) → *escutai-me depressa* |
| propter | por causa de | working | Ps 5:9 *por causa dos meus inimigos*, Ps 6:5 *por causa da vossa misericórdia* (MS1932 *pela*) |
formulas: | *Dómine, ne in furóre tuo árguas me, * neque in ira tua corrípias me* (6:2 = 37:2, word for word) | *Senhor, não me acuseis no vosso furor, * nem me castigueis na vossa ira* | open (hangs on *árguere*, *corrípere*) — Ps 6; **Ps 37 copies it**. It opens the first and the third Penitential Psalm |
| *Convértere, Dómine* (6:5, 89:13; 79:15 *Deus virtútum, convértere*) | *Voltai-vos, Senhor* | open (hangs on *convértere*) — Ps 6 |

| *Discédite a me, omnes, qui operámini iniquitátem* (6:9) | *Afastai-vos de mim, todos vós que praticais a iniquidade* | working — Ps 6; the Gospel quotes it (Mt 7:23 — from memory, unverified); 118:115 *Declináte a me, malígni* is another verb (*Apartai-vos*) |
| *ossa mea conturbáta sunt* (6:3, 30:11) | *os meus ossos estão perturbados* | open (hangs on *conturbáre*) — Ps 6 |
